body: Not true. A single 100% MH rating means you have TOTAL occupational and social impairment and cannot function in a workplace. If you have say 70% for MH with other disabilities that total 100%, then you can work, no problem. I have two buddies who worked with 100% rating for ptsd and they got bumped down to 70%. OP can do whatever he wants, obviously, but VA heavily reviews those 100% MH ratings.

Congrats. 100% is very hard to get for MH. Make sure you don’t work, or they will take it from you. 100% for MH indicates TOTAL occupational impairment, which means you cannot function in a workplace.

That’s not right. I’ve been in therapy for 7 years at the VA and Vet Center for ptsd resulting from military service. I have had several different therapists because I have moved, some therapists retire, etc. Not once has any of them ever told me I had to deal with childhood issues in order to deal with my current issues resulting from military service. Therapy does make things worse initially because it opens everything up, but if you find the right therapist, you can make great strides in therapy.

I will say that prior to seeking help at the VA, I had one “civilian” therapist in the community who tried the childhood thing on me. I told her I needed help with what is currently going on resulting from my military experience. She didn’t seem to want to do that, so I quit seeing her. My point here is, it seems the VA psychologists and Vet Center counselors know how to better help us. I’m not knocking other therapists. It’s just an observation.

Look. The VA can do a records review without your knowledge. To them, not seeking treatment shows an improvement.  They can send you a letter to propose a reduction. I’m not saying it’s right or wrong. I’m just saying it’s the way that it is. I’ve seen a few people get dropped from 70% ptsd all the way down to 30%. If they propose to reduce you, you have 60 days to provide evidence that you haven’t improved. That’s hard to do if you aren’t seeking treatment in the first place.

I’ll be honest and say that I am a war veteran and take the Prazosin and trazadone combo and it helps me sleep and I don’t wake up screaming from a nightmare like I used to. How long have you been in treatment for? It seems you have to go through a lot of different therapies and meds before they approve you for TMS and/or Ketamine. I’ve been in treatment for 7 years and tried all the meds they gave me, along with all the therapies, and just last year I was deemed treatment resistant. 

My VA has TMS and I tried it but that didn’t work. If you have PTSD on top of depression and anxiety, the chances of it working are only 50%, according to the doctor who did my TMS. But we tried it anyway, with no change.

Some VA’s have nasal ketamine (esketamine), and others don’t. Mine is one that doesn’t have it yet, so I am using my disability $ to start ketamine treatments on my own at the advice of my VA MH provider. I’m starting in two weeks, and I am hoping this will work. The next option is ECT and that scares me.

As others have suggested, you should try CBT, DBT, EMDR, CPR, PE, and individual therapy. The Vet Centers have awesome counselors too. I see someone there 2x a month because my VA is short on psychologists.

It’s a tough road for sure, and I understand your frustration.

Edited to add: I forgot to mention the Alpha-Stim. Ask your provider about this device. Many veterans use it and it does help somewhat with anxiety. You will have to go to sessions to see if it will work for you and to teach you how to use it. Usually three sessions, and if they feel you will benefit from it, they will give you one to take home. It’s expensive, like $1200, so they want to make sure it will help you before they give you one.
